description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(llm): continue a thinking turn the provider ends mid-thought

Some Gemini models answer one request with at most a segment of
thinking -- measured, about 32k thinking tokens and seven minutes at
the highest effort -- then stop with finish reason CONTINUATION and a
continuation token. The same request sent again with the token
continues the turn; the request's output ceiling counts across the
segments. The Google GenAI SDK re-sends the token itself. LiteLLM at
the pinned version does not: it drops the token and maps the finish
reason to "stop", so the turn reached the harness as a thought with no
answer and the stage ended with nothing. Measured: a hard problem at
the highest effort returned 65,536 tokens of thinking and no text.

The token is surfaced by a wrapper on LiteLLM's candidate processing,
the one point both whole and streamed responses pass through, which
copies the token and the raw finish reason into the message's
provider-specific fields and maps CONTINUATION to a length stop. The
client layer that already sees LiteLLM's responses raw then continues
the turn: the identical request again with the token on the body's top
level (LiteLLM's extra_body), each segment through the same retries as
the first. A whole response folds the segments into one (text and
reasoning joined, tool calls and finish reason from the last, usage
summed, cached counts included); a stream delivers them as one stream,
the finishes and usage of the segments in between withheld and the
turn's usage summed on the final usage chunk, so ADK aggregates one
turn. Only a CONTINUATION stop continues; a MAX_TOKENS stop means the
request's own ceiling is spent, and is left as it is.

A turn is continued until the provider ends it, with the answer or
with MAX_TOKENS when the request's output ceiling -- cumulative across
segments, and the operator's to set -- is spent; ending it sooner
would throw every segment's work away with nothing to show, so there
is no cap of this code's own by default. Two bounds remain. The run's
budget is consulted before each segment, with the turn's own spend so
far added to what has been metered, since the pipeline meters a turn
only when it ends: a run that cannot afford the next segment ends the
turn where it is and pauses on the usual path, resumable. And
MANTIS_MAX_CONTINUATIONS lets an operator cap one turn's segments
anyway (0, the default, is no cap). Each continuation is counted in
the spend report, and each notice says what the finished segment used,
cached tokens included. A LiteLLM that surfaces the token itself is
left alone, and a turn it has already continued carries no token, so
a later upgrade makes this inert rather than doubled.

Change-Id: I41a18bcb9e9469a29d1d1451e4518eac851d9abc
